source.title: Learning Neural Networks with Adaptive Regularization
source.authors: Han Zhao; Yao-Hung Hubert Tsai; R. Salakhutdinov; G. Gordon

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present; no evident truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests explicit adaptive regularization and measured network properties against held-out generalization on natural-label datasets, but does not test the specific mechanisms in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for adaptive regularization and comparisons with weight decay, dropout, batch normalization, and DeCov. Its citations to other studies on batch size and generalization are prior work, not this paper's results. The stable-rank and spectral-norm values are presented in figures without recoverable numerical values.
record.test_reason: The CNN dropout comparisons directly test V6 using held-out classification accuracy. The study also compares batch sizes relevant to V5, but does not establish a fixed epoch budget for the main accuracy experiments. Adaptive regularization is not an adaptive-optimizer comparison, and spectral norms and stable ranks are not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that AdaReg improves generalization on MNIST, CIFAR10 and SARCOS and yields smaller stable ranks and spectral norms. They interpret these properties as explaining the improvement; the experiments do not independently establish that causal explanation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an adaptive matrix-normal-prior regularizer and block coordinate descent; evaluates natural-label classification and multitask regression, not the memorization, optimizer, or sharpness interventions in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset size and minibatch size affect classification results; batch normalization deteriorates at large batch size on CIFAR10 but is not batch-size-sensitive on MNIST. Applying AdaReg only to the softmax layer generalizes best among the tested layer placements. Combination with batch normalization can further improve results; combination with dropout shows no significant difference on this dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaReg improves classification generalization relative to tested regularizers as training-set size grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning a matrix-normal regularizer for the final layer can improve MNIST and CIFAR10 held-out classification performance.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaReg raises explained variance over unregularized MTL on all seven SARCOS tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive final-layer regularization can improve held-out multitask regression performance.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaReg lowers final-layer stable rank and spectral norm alongside improved held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower final-layer stable ranks and spectral norms can accompany improved generalization under adaptive regularization.

record.problems: The paper evaluates only the final softmax layer for its main classification experiments and does not test memorization of random labels. Exact classification accuracies and stable-rank/spectral-norm values in the figures are not stated in text. The reported result uncertainty is standard deviation across repetitions for some plots; regression-table uncertainty is not stated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning-dependent differences.

Fixed epoch budgets for the main accuracy comparisons are unspecified. No workload-dependent batch threshold, longer-training intervention, or learning-rate scaling and warmup comparison is established.

Fully connected classification, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. The supplied figure text does not resolve dropout's effect separately on very small training sets.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons against alternative measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Add dropout-versus-no-dropout comparisons on top of AdaReg for MNIST at batch sizes 256 and 2048. The authors report no significant difference; record this as absent incremental benefit.

Record explicit paired batch-size contrasts: BN deteriorates on CIFAR10 but is insensitive on MNIST; AdaReg is reported insensitive while most methods suffer. Identify the main accuracy experiment's epoch budgets before issuing a fixed-budget verdict.

record.verdict_notes: No listed original source is this study. Exact Figure 2 curves cannot be reconstructed from the supplied text, but explicit qualitative results remain usable. V5 receives no verdict because the main accuracy experiments' fixed epoch budgets are unverified; the budget described for Figure 3's optimization experiment cannot automatically be assigned to Figure 2. States for rows linked to no version describe their inability to establish a listed claim, not a denial of the reported numerical changes.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects across dataset sizes and configurations; combined removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the test-accuracy effect.
